pr_title: Fix building bibs not blocking placement.
pr_body:
Fixes #18816, which was regressed by #18688 removing the `BuildingInfluence` check from `BuildingUtils.IsCellBuildable`. 
Fixes #18840.

Bib cells are not added to the `ActorMap`, so were no longer being considered for blocking building placement. This PR solves the regression by adding a new set of methods to explicitly track cells that are blocked for building.
pr_comments:
Considering #18852, we should instead revert #18689 and then change `BuildingUtils.IsCellBuildable` to query the BuildingMap again (there is no need to throw out the other improvements from #18688).

I have filed #18853 outling what I believe to be the better long term solution, which is too big to do in this release cycle.

issue_context.title: Bot places buildings on bibs and exits blocking itself
comments: This is going to be a regression from #18689. The bib cells are probably not being considered in the ActorMap.

Yeah the footprints might be broken

review_comments: This is a bit weird. You are only removing it for real if nothing is left so that the removal is complete (all or nothing)? Why is this necessary?

We are taking advantage of the fact that the total number of blocked cells on the map is small and sparse to use a dictionary of (blocked cell) → (list of blockers) instead of having to define an entire `CellLayer`. We can then simply check if the dictionary contains the cell key - if any values are defined then the cell is blocked, and we don't care about *what* is blocking.

When we remove an item we do care about what is blocking, and if this was the last blocker we need to remove the empty list so that the `ContainsKey` check can correctly return false.

On a deeper look, I don't think this is correct. `IsBuildingBlocked` is supposed to have an effect on `AllowInvalidPlacement`: the expected behaviour is that those cells should show red on the placement preview; the overall placement is allowed, but those specific tiles are ignored.

The suggested changes regress the concrete placement behaviour in d2k: hovering the concrete PBOG over a building that that was built on concrete correctly shows red, but hovering the concrete PBOG over a building that was built on rock shows white!

In the longer term (i'm not sure its feasible for the upcoming playtest) it would probably be better to use the yellow placement tiles instead of red in this case - red is supposed to mean that the placement is not allowed at all, whereas yellow means it is allowed but those specific cells are going to behave differently.

If we can get this and #18685 merged in a reasonable time we can look into the feasibility of removing `AllowInvalidPlacement` from building and instead introducing a new `D2kConcrete` trait that can be placed using PBOG but behaves like `AllowInvalidPlacement` and has the special case handling for yellow tiles in `D2kActorPreviewPlaceBuildingPreview`.

> The suggested changes regress the concrete placement behaviour in d2k: hovering the concrete PBOG over a building that that was built on concrete correctly shows red, but hovering the concrete PBOG over a building that was built on rock shows white!

I actually expected something like this, and think it would be better to always show white not red, simply because a full red preview won't block you from placing it down (when you would expect it to reject placement; I think we have an open issue for that). I guess this doesn't matter if we remove `AllowInvalidPlacement` in the long run.
My idea of a specific `D2kConcrete` and PBOG/preview handling could fix that too.

Btw, I just remembered what is going on here. Whatever we do in this method is kind of a moot point because of https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/blob/daa8c74c375d88999fa4671cecb45fe4222d2548/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildings/BuildingUtils.cs#L76-L79
Which means returning false here just results in a red color that is completely ignored.
Indeed. That's what I said above 😄
